files.summary: Add redirect limit, blocklist, DNS options
Add blocklist and DNS private-address check
Optional absolute ExpiresAt on create request
Redirect rate limit with 429 + Retry-After; expired flag
Wire validator options and redirect limiter

compatibilityRisks: API: CreateLinkRequest gains an optional trailing ExpiresAt, and LinkMetadataResponse gains a trailing IsExpired field. Both are additive JSON changes.

Behaviour: GET /r/{code} and GET /{code} can now return 429 after 600 requests per minute per remote IP. Tests that redirect more than that from one IP will fail unless they raise RedirectRateLimitPerWindow.

Behaviour: DNS resolution at creation is enabled by default, so POST /api/urls does a real lookup. Lookups are bounded by DnsTimeoutMilliseconds (2 s). Unresolvable or timed-out hosts are allowed (fail open, a deviation from the design's fail-closed). Set DnsResolutionEnabled=false for offline tests.
Security: DNS rebinding after creation is not detected. The redirect limiter keys on the remote IP, so clients behind a shared proxy share one limit. Trusted-proxy header handling is not implemented.
Performance: DNS lookups use a blocking wait on the request thread, which is acceptable only for the low-volume creation path. The redirect path adds one in-memory limiter lookup.
Data: no schema change. In-memory state and rate-limit counters are per instance and lost on restart.
alreadySatisfied: FR-2/FR-3: the bounded click queue with a non-blocking TryWrite and a background ClickProcessor already exists. The click is enqueued only on the successful 302 path, so 404, 410 and 429 are not counted.
FR-1/FR-5: a past or invalid expiry via expiresInMinutes returns 400. An expired link returns 410 on redirect. Metadata for an expired link already returns 200.
FR-3: GET /api/urls/{code}/analytics and /stats already return 200, or 404 for an unknown code.
FR-4: the scheme allowlist, credential rejection, and the literal loopback/private/link-local checks (IPv4, IPv6 and IPv4-mapped) already exist.
FR-6: creation rate limiting with Retry-After and per-client windows with purge already exists.
note: Proposed by the developer agent. NOT applied to the repository; validated in a sandbox and exported for human review.
